content: Cefmetazole is classified as a cephamycin antibiotic and is typically grouped with second-generation cephalosporins. The chemical structure of cefmetazole includes an N-methylthiotetrazole (NMTT or 1-MTT) side chain. During the metabolic breakdown of cefmetazole in the body, free NMTT is released. This compound has been associated with hypoprothrombinemia, which is likely caused by the inhibition of the enzyme vitamin K epoxide reductase. Additionally, NMTT can induce a disulfiram-like reaction when ethanol is consumed, due to its inhibition of aldehyde dehydrogenase. Cefmetazole exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and has demonstrated efficacy in treating infections caused by bacteria such as those responsible for urinary tract infections and skin infections. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) data for certain clinically significant microorganisms are as follows: Bacteroides fragilis: MIC ranges from 0.06 to >256 µg/ml. Clostridium difficile: MIC ranges from 8 to >128 µg/ml. Staphylococcus aureus (including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus or MRSA): MIC ranges from 0.5 to 256 µg/ml.
